clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 1  of the act of August 1, 
1914, 38 Stat. 609, 623 (U. S. C., title 
19, sec. 2), Executive Order No. 83231  of 
January 22, 1940, abolishing Customs 
Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee); 
revoking the designations of Memphis, 
Chattanooga, and Nashville, Tennessee, 
as customs ports of entry; extending the 
limits of Customs Collection District No. 
42 (Kentucky) to include the State of 
Tennessee; and extending the limits of 
Customs Collection District No. 45 (St. 
Louis) to include the State of Arkansas, 
is hereby revoked.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 8341 of February 8, 1940 (5 FR 643, Federal Register issue of February 10, 1940) is a one-paragraph order whose only operative act is to revoke Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which had abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee), revoked the designations of Memphis, Chattanooga and Nashville as customs ports of entry, and extended the limits of District No. 42 (Kentucky) and District No. 45 (St. Louis). The held text says the earlier order "is hereby revoked." The act has no deferred effective date, condition, report or continuing duty, so it was performed and exhausted when signed on February 8, 1940. No instrument held in the repository revokes, amends or extends Executive Order 8341, so no earlier or later end displaces that date. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription; the page number and date were read from it.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists: the order is itself a revocation executed on signing, with no stated later effective date, so nothing precedes February 8, 1940. The date is the signing date, which the held text gives as \"February 8, 1940.\" Under 44 U.S.C. 1507 a document required to be published is not valid against a person without actual knowledge until filed; the held text shows filing on February 9, 1940, and the issue date is February 10, 1940. The alternative readings (filing or issue date) are disclosed; none changes the conclusion that the revocation was performed in the first days of February 1940. The packet's later-event chain is empty, the machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes covering 1937 onward) return zero hits for this order, and the bounded held-text search found no later order citing it by number.","independent_command_check":"The order contains no independent command, delegation, reporting duty or continuing instruction. The only operative content is the revocation of Executive Order No. 8323, and that content is exhausted when the revocation took effect.","savings_check":"The order has no savings clause. Its consequence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 8323, is a surviving effect of an executed act, not an unperformed command of Executive Order 8341, and no held source shows any separate duty, right or pending action left by it.","scope_check":"The packet inventory has one clause (the sole paragraph, characters 1046 to 1635 of the registered text), which I confirmed against the whole held order: heading, the single operative paragraph, signature, date and Federal Register filing line. There is no second section, so the inventory is complete. The one clause is a one-time revocation, terminated by performance on February 8, 1940."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 was executed on February 8, 1940. The order has no savings clause and the held searches show no later instrument touching it.
